application.tagline: Front-end-only reconstruction of the Vodafone Qatar CRM/CVM Digital Experience Platform
application.repository: local blueprint (blueprint/reconstruction-package/) — no live codebase exists yet

executive_summary:
The Vodafone Qatar DXP is a planned replacement for the legacy Siebel/ECR/VSA CRM stack, rebuilt here as a production-ready, front-end-only React application: no APIs, backend services, databases, or third-party integrations. Every workflow, business rule, validation, permission, calculation, approval, and state transition is simulated entirely in front-end logic.

The platform serves 66 evidenced personas (retail sales agents, fulfilment agents, managers/approvers, credit control, back office, and more) across 16 functional modules — Lead Management, Mobile Postpaid/Prepaid, Fixed Line/Fibre, FWA/5G Home, MNP/FNP Porting, Enterprise/IoT/B2B, Billing & Adjustments, Order Management, Identity & Customer Management, SIM & Number Management, Trouble Ticketing, Access/Roles/Approval Governance, CAF/Attachments & Forms, and Platform Governance — comprising 213 screens built from 111 end-to-end user journeys.

This document's two diagrams are synthesized from a 4-stage evidence-backed reconstruction blueprint (`blueprint/`), not from a scan of existing code — no implementation exists yet. The Technical Architecture diagram shows the recommended system shape (5 simulation engines standing in for what a real backend/auth-server/rules-engine would normally provide). The Information Architecture diagram shows the navigation hierarchy (16 modules → sub-modules → screens) and the core entity relationships underlying the domain model.
technology_overview: No target tech stack is evidenced anywhere in the 83-document source corpus (the corpus's only UI evidence is screenshots of the legacy Siebel/Open UI system being replaced). Every technology below is therefore a recommended default from the Stage D architecture blueprint (`blueprint/reconstruction-package/docs/frontend-architecture.md`), not a confirmed fact — see `assumptions`.

technical_architecture.narrative: There is no backend by design (per the project's front-end-only constraint). Five simulation engines take the place of what a real backend/rules-engine/auth-server would normally provide, each reading from generated, evidence-backed configuration JSON rather than hardcoded logic: the Configuration Engine loads all config at boot; the Persona Engine simulates authentication/authorization by filtering navigation and screen/action visibility against the RBAC Matrix (145 evidenced entries); the Rule Engine evaluates the 346-entry Business Rule catalogue (eligibility, thresholds, calculations); the Validation Engine evaluates the 418-entry Validation catalogue at the field level; and the Mock Data Engine simulates CRUD persistence (with artificial latency and referential-integrity checks) against IndexedDB, standing in for a real database. Screen components (organized into 16 modules) compose a small set of shared UI patterns rather than being built bespoke — see `blueprint/reconstruction-package/docs/reusable-patterns.md`'s 18 evidence-backed patterns.

components.name: Screen Components (16 modules, 213 screens)
components.responsibility: Compose shared UI patterns into the catalogued screens; no bespoke business logic — delegates to the engines below

components.name: Navigation / Router
components.responsibility: Client-side routing generated from routes.json; sidebar/breadcrumb navigation filtered by the active persona

components.name: Persona Engine
components.responsibility: Simulates authentication/authorization: tracks the active persona and filters visible routes/actions via the RBAC Matrix (no real login exists)

components.name: Rule Engine
components.responsibility: Evaluates business rules (eligibility, thresholds, calculations) from business-rules.json; falls back to a visible dev-mode warning for any rule without a registered implementation

components.name: Validation Engine
components.technology: TypeScript module + React Hook Form resolvers
components.responsibility: Evaluates field-level validation rules from validation-rules.json against the 970-entry Field Inventory

components.name: Mock Data Engine
components.responsibility: Simulates a backend: CRUD operations with artificial latency, referential-integrity checks, and entity lifecycle-state transitions, entirely in-browser

components.name: Configuration Engine
components.responsibility: Boot-time loader exposing typed accessors over all config/*.json — no screen imports config JSON directly

components.name: Zustand Stores
components.responsibility: In-memory application state, one store per bounded context (persona, entity, workflow, notification, config)

components.name: Browser Persistence (IndexedDB / localStorage / sessionStorage)
components.responsibility: Durability layer standing in for a real database — survives reloads within a session

data_flows.description: Filters visible modules/routes/actions by the active persona's RBAC entries
Resolves field-level validation rules per screen/field before submit
Evaluates eligibility/threshold/calculation business rules (e.g. Bill Limit Agent Minimum) during a guided journey
CRUD reads/writes against the simulated backend (customers, accounts, orders, tickets, leads)
Persists entity records; enforces evidenced lifecycle-state transitions (e.g. Billing Profile: good standing → overdue → in collection → blacklisted)
Persists active persona and in-progress wizard/journey draft state

technical_architecture.deployment: Static single-page application, built with Vite, deployable to any static host or CDN (e.g. object storage + CDN) — no server runtime, container, or database is required at any environment tier. This is an architectural consequence of the project's explicit front-end-only constraint, not evidenced by the source corpus (which describes the legacy Siebel/ECR/VSA deployment, being replaced, not the new DXP's deployment target). CI/CD would be a standard static-build-and-deploy pipeline.

information_architecture.narrative: The application's information architecture is Platform → Module → Sub-Module → Screen → Component → Action, derived from the 16-module hierarchy synthesized from 111 journeys, 308 requirements, and 83 entities (`blueprint/module-hierarchy.md`). Primary navigation is the 16 modules (sidebar, filtered by the active persona's RBAC entries); secondary navigation is a module's sub-modules and screens. Screen-to-module assignment (`blueprint/reconstruction-package/config/routes.json`) is a deterministic keyword match against each module's capability list — a strong starting point, not a confirmed final IA. Full screen-by-screen detail (213 entries) lives in `blueprint/screens.md`; this diagram shows the module/sub-module tier with representative screen counts rather than all 213 leaf nodes, which would not be legible in a single diagram. (The diagram below shows the Platform → Module tier only, for legibility; the Module → Sub-Module → Screen tier is detailed in the navigation table above and in full in `blueprint/module-hierarchy.md` and `blueprint/screens.md`.)

assumptions: No live codebase exists yet — both diagrams are synthesized from the Stage A-D evidence-backed reconstruction blueprint (`blueprint/`), not from static analysis of a repository. Treat this document as a design specification, not an as-built record.

The entire technology_inventory (React, TypeScript, Vite, Zustand, React Hook Form, Tailwind CSS) is a recommended default from `blueprint/reconstruction-package/docs/frontend-architecture.md` §1 — no source document specifies a target tech stack.

Screen-to-module assignment in the Information Architecture navigation tree is a deterministic keyword match (`config/routes.json`), not a confirmed final IA — expect some screens to need manual re-bucketing.
The Entity Relationship Diagram shows 14 of 83 evidenced entities, curated for diagram legibility (8-20 node guidance) by module-hierarchy reference frequency — not the full domain model.
The 'Customer' node in the ERD merges two closely related legacy entity variants (ENT-023 Customer, ENT-037 Customer/Contact) found in the source corpus — see `domain-model.md` for the distinction.

Deployment description (static SPA, no server) is an architectural consequence of the explicit front-end-only project constraint, not evidenced by the source corpus, which only describes the legacy system being replaced.
confidence_notes: High confidence on the module/screen/entity counts and relationships (all evidence-cited in blueprint/*.md, traceable to specific source documents). Low-to-no confidence on the specific technology choices and deployment target (Assumed defaults, explicitly flagged, since the source corpus contains no target-state technical specification — only legacy-system screenshots and business/functional requirements).
